RagShortTexts: The standing military of Burgundians in 374 AD relied upon veteran formations specialized in disciplined field deployment.
Combining heavy protective armor with specialized assault weaponry, the troops executed tactical doctrines honed in frontier engagements.
Commanders emphasized coordinated shock charges and defensive stability, preventing frontline collapse against aggressive cavalry raids.

Variants.Content: The martial renown of Burgundians rested upon exhaustive drilling and veteran battlefield cohesion during the turbulent close of the 4th century. Core tactical doctrine integrated heavy shield formations with disciplined skirmishing wings, executing tactical maneuvers designed to absorb and counter enemy shock. Along vulnerable sectors, defensive engineers implemented field fortifications and obstacles, breaking the initial momentum of hostile assaults. Once enemy ranks faltered, armored shock reserves counter-charged under thunderous horn blasts, crushing exposed flanks with heavy swords and barbed spears. This balance of resilient endurance and ferocious striking power formed the military bedrock preserving Burgundians against overwhelming regional adversaries.

Front-line men lower their shields and set their feet in the wet grass as the enemy horsemen crest the rise. Those behind push spears through the gaps, shouting to one another until the charge breaks against the wall. A line that holds is the only hope for the wounded men lying in the rear.

The war council has placed the heavy foot in the center and sent the riders around the river flank to strike the enemy's rear. The grain convoy must cross the bridge before the enemy blocks the road. Give the order to the captains in person, because a written plan will be copied by the river chiefs and passed to the enemy scouts.
